full_sentence: Look at those dark clouds! It is going to rain.
acceptable_variants: It is probably going to rain soon.

options.text: I am going to visit my aunt.
options.why_wrong: This is a plan about a visit and has no connection to the clouds, so it does not follow from the evidence in the stem.
'Yesterday' is a past time, but 'will' expresses the future. The two parts of this sentence do not match.
This contradicts the dark clouds in the stem and does not make a prediction based on them.

grammar_focus: Going to for predictions based on present evidence
explanation: When the speaker can see evidence now, such as dark clouds, we use the going to future to make a prediction. Learners who use only the will future for every prediction may miss this difference in meaning.
translation: ¡Mira esas nubes oscuras! Va a llover.
